call_points.text: No revenue or profitability guidance for FY27 due to geopolitical uncertainty.
Bid pipeline of ₹1.5 lakh Cr for the next nine months; ₹3.96 lakh Cr over two years.
Overseas projects carry 200-300 bps higher margins than domestic.
UP Jal Jeevan Mission receivables of close to ₹400 Cr remain largely unpaid.
Management declined to give absolute gross debt or working capital days, citing unaudited numbers.
Croatia and Vadhavan projects will see minuscule turnover this year; Croatia picks up next year.
HSR tunneling turnover to commence from November; force majeure settlement expected this quarter.
Management has withheld specific revenue and margin guidance for FY27 due to geopolitical uncertainties.
Total capex for FY27 is projected at around ₹725 crores.
No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance given in the presentation.
Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6.1% from 12.2% a year earlier.

operating_notes.text: Secured ₹373 Cr EPC and TBM tunneling order in April 2026 under Urban Infrastructure and Metro BU.
Secured intimation as the most suitable bidder for a railway rehabilitation and construction project in Croatia valued at €677.07 million (~₹7,544 Cr) excluding taxes.
Croatian Motorways Ltd cancelled road packages J324/23 and J325/23 because offer prices exceeded planned financial resources.
Order book ₹32,496 Cr at Mar'26; Urban Infra 51%, Hydro & Underground 23%, Marine & Industrial 15%, Surface Transport 9%, Oil & Gas 2%.
Strategic equipment fleet worth ₹4,282.55 Cr as of Mar'26, including 20 TBMs and 142 cranes.
FY26 order inflow stood at ₹4,125 Cr excluding variations and change orders of approximately ₹3,800 Cr.
Order book of ₹43,290 Cr at end-Q1FY27; ₹15,695 Cr booked to date, with no L1 orders pending conversion.
Bid pipeline of ₹1.5 lakh Cr for the next nine months and ₹3.96 lakh Cr over two years.
Around 11% of order book is slow-moving or stalled (5.65% slow-moving, 2% Bangladesh, 3% Jal Jeevan Mission).
₹35 Cr unsecured CP issued at 8.10% for 77 days, rated Crisil A1+, placed with Ambit Finvest Pvt Ltd.
India Ratings assigned IND AA-/Stable to ₹250 Cr proposed NCDs and affirmed IND A1+ on ₹500 Cr commercial paper.
Challenging a ₹77.65 Cr GST demand (tax and penalty) for FY18 and FY19 at the GST Appellate Tribunal.

timeline.summary: Afcons Infrastructure secured a ₹373 Cr EPC and TBM tunneling order under its Urban Infrastructure and Metro BU in April 2026.
Afcons Infrastructure announced selection as the preferred bidder for a ₹7,544 Cr railway rehabilitation and construction project in Croatia.

Afcons Infrastructure Ltd announces Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call on May 19, 2026, at 11:00 AM (IST) with **Subramanian Krishnamurthy**, **Srinivasan Paramasivan**, **Ramesh Kumar Jha**, and **Hitesh Singh** presenting.
Croatian Motorways cancelled two road construction tenders (Packages J324/23 and J325/23) where Afcons Infrastructure was the L1 bidder.
Afcons Infrastructure clarified on May 18, 2026, that Croatian Motorways cancelled two road tenders while its railway bid in Croatia remains under consideration.
Afcons Infrastructure filed its Q4 & FY26 investor presentation on May 18, 2026: FY26 total income ₹12,322 Cr (-5.4%), PAT ₹251 Cr (-48.5%), order book ₹32,496 Cr.
Afcons Infrastructure Limited uploaded Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call recording on May 19, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. (IST) via its website.
Afcons Infrastructure reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹2,777 Cr and a net loss of ₹89 Cr, withdrawing FY27 guidance amid geopolitical and liquidity headwinds.
Zahan C Mistry, Promoter of Afcons Infrastructure Ltd, declared no new encumbrances by promoter group under SEBI SAST Regulations for FY2025-26 on April 06, 2026.
Afcons Infrastructure issued ₹25 Cr of commercial paper at 8.05% maturing on December 3, 2026.
On 10 August 2026, Afcons held its Q1FY27 earnings call, reporting revenue of ₹2,727 Cr (down 20.3% YoY), EBITDA of ₹263 Cr (9.6% margin) and PAT of ₹30 Cr, with an order book of ₹43,290 Cr.
Afcons Infrastructure issued ₹35 Cr of unsecured commercial paper on October 13, 2026 at 8.10%, rated Crisil A1+, maturing December 29, 2026.
On 15 October 2026, Afcons disclosed that India Ratings assigned IND AA-/Stable to its ₹250 Cr proposed NCDs and affirmed IND A1+ on its ₹500 Cr commercial paper.
Afcons Infrastructure received an appellate order confirming a ₹77.65 Cr GST demand and penalty for the 2017-2019 period, which it plans to contest at GSTAT.
